1.why: GET /api/mfa/settings and recovery endpoints require authenticated(s) with s.account and stage === 'mfa', so MFA data is only served for the signed-in session owner.

2.why: Identity challenges are stored per identity target and authenticator/recovery secrets are bound to the session; a code for one user/target does not validate for a different user.

3.why: Enabling MFA only updates the current session’s stage to 'mfa' and never invalidates other existing sessions in the sessions map.

4.why: OTP shared secret is stored as AES-GCM encryptedSecret; backup codes are stored only as SHA-256 hashes with recoveryPepper.

5.why: All secrets and codes are generated via crypto.getRandomValues (randomBytes, randomDecimalCode, randomRecoveryCode, session ids).

6.why: Session id is only in an HttpOnly cookie; client script keeps csrf in memory and never writes secrets/OTPs/tokens to localStorage, sessionStorage, or non-HttpOnly cookies.

7.why: Server validates email/phone (validatedIdentity), OTP (validOtp), authenticator secret (validSecret), and recovery codes (validRecovery) before use.

8.why: Dynamic DOM updates use textContent; HTML is fixed with CSP nonces and API data is JSON, so injected markup is not executed.

9.why: The app performs no HTTP redirects at all, so there is neither an open redirect nor an explicit redirect allow-list implementation.

10.why: baseHeaders sets CSP, Strict-Transport-Security, X-Content-Type-Options, and X-Frame-Options/frame-ancestors 'none'.

11.why: cookieFor sets mfa_session with HttpOnly, Secure, and SameSite=Strict.

12.why: Errors are generic with no stack traces and tokens are not in URLs, but mock testOtp and recovery codes are returned in API JSON and written to the on-page Logs panel.

13.why: Identity challenge has used + expiresAt (CHALLENGE_MS); authenticator confirm is single-use; recovery codes are removed on use; TOTP is time-stepped.

14.why: failedAttempt locks identity/authenticator/recovery after 5 failures for LOCKOUT_MS; mayAttempt enforces the lockout.

15.why: Session id is rotated on sign-in and identity verify, idle/absolute timeouts are enforced in sessionFrom, and logout deletes the session and expires the cookie.
